$comment: The platform configuration the ratification mechanism's trust argument depends on, committed IN THE REPOSITORY so that changing the EXPECTATION is itself a reviewable governance diff rather than a settings change nobody sees. Written 2026-09-10 to the specification of an AI council (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, 2/2 convergent, 2 rounds, blind peer review) under a written owner delegation, resolving blocker `ratification-platform-anchor` of `agents/roadmaps/road-to-typed-grants-that-persist.md`. Both seats required that only generic evaluation logic live in code and that this file sit on the gated-surface list, so a policy-only edit reds `check_kernel_edit_ratified` without its own ratification. openai additionally required a non-negotiable floor embedded in the verifier itself, so that an edit HERE cannot lower a threshold and make itself green; that floor is `NON_NEGOTIABLE_FLOOR` in `src/scripts/_lib/platform_anchor.ts` and this file is rejected when it falls below it. SCHEMA 2, 2026-09-10: the field set changed — the two approval keys are gone by owner ruling and `accepted_risk_reductions` arrived — so the version moved with it rather than leaving a reader to discover the shape had changed under a constant number.

accepted_risk_reductions.failure_mode: Semantic conflict. With strictness off a branch may merge on checks that passed against a base it has not caught up with, and the staleness is not bounded to one commit — any number of merges may have landed since. Two independently green branches can therefore compose into a broken base although neither was broken alone.
accepted_risk_reductions.cost_avoided: Sequential rebase plus a full re-run per branch before each merge. Measured on this repository during the 2026-09-10 session: the matrix runs 34 to 45 checks and `ci_settle` needed three 9-minute passes on several branches, so ~20-30 minutes per re-run and roughly an hour for three green branches merged back to back.
accepted_risk_reductions.frequency_assumption: ASSUMPTION, owner-attested, NOT a measurement: the owner states such breakage 'happens too rarely' to outweigh the re-run cost. No incident data supports or refutes it yet, and this field is worded as an assumption deliberately — presenting it as a measured rate would be the kind of overstatement this file exists to prevent.
accepted_risk_reductions.detection_and_repair: Post-merge. The breakage surfaces on the next `main` run of the affected workflow, or on the next branch that inherits it; the owner repairs it in a follow-up. The owner accepted this explicitly: 'If something breaks in the process, I can fix it afterwards.'
accepted_risk_reductions.residual_protection: `Sync + Generate Tools Consistency` stays a REQUIRED status check and must still pass, so no branch merges without the ratification gate having run. What that does not prove is compatibility with the current base — a required check certifies the commit it ran on, never the merge result.
review_triggers: the first attributable stale-base semantic conflict, reviewed immediately
median end-to-end required-check duration falls below 10 minutes over 30 days — the cost half of this trade-off then collapses
merge-queue or rebase-on-merge tooling removes the repeated re-runs
automatic expiry 2026-12-09; renewal is a fresh decision with refreshed measurements, never an extension

accepted_risk_note: THE FLOOR IS NOW TWO TIERS, and this file says so rather than implying otherwise. Six dimensions are hard — `NEVER_WAIVABLE` in `src/scripts/_lib/platform_anchor.ts`: enforcement, target, default-branch coverage, unconditional bypass, deletion and force-push. The rest are baseline expectations a complete, unexpired, owner-authorised waiver may trade against a documented operational benefit. Calling that 'the non-negotiable floor unchanged' would be false; it is a 6-dimension hard floor plus trade-offable dimensions with documentation requirements. WHY A THIRD STATE rather than deletion or a permanent red: deleting a dimension the repository still considers safer erases the difference between 'never expected' and 'expected and knowingly waived', while an enforced-and-red dimension makes the gate report a policy violation when the policy is what chose the configuration. openai: 'If noncompliance does not fail the gate, that dimension is not enforced for the duration of the waiver. It remains a baseline expectation subject to an active exception.' WHAT STOPS THIS BECOMING AN EXEMPTION REGISTRY, which both seats warned it would: eligibility is bounded by a committed list rather than by the quality of a waiver's prose; every field is required and an incomplete waiver is REFUSED rather than honoured, so the dimension it names reds normally; a waiver past `expires` is not honoured; and a waiver for a dimension the forge already satisfies is reported as stale. A malformed waiver is worse than no waiver, never better. DECIDED BY: the owner on the policy; an AI council (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, 2 rounds, blind peer review, 2/2 convergent) on this shape, which both seats reached after rejecting outright removal AND a permanent red.
required_status_check_contexts_note: The context that CARRIES the ratification gate, not the gate's own script name. `check_kernel_edit_ratified` is a STEP inside the `Sync + Generate Tools Consistency` job (`.github/workflows/consistency.yml:811-825`), and a GitHub required status check pins a job's reported context, never the steps inside it. This distinction is load-bearing and was corrected mid-decision: the council question asserted that the gate 'is not a required status check at all', which measurement then falsified — the containing job IS the ruleset's one required context. What survives the correction, and what the round-2 ratification review actually refused the deny-retirement over, is that pinning a job name does not pin its steps: a candidate branch may delete the gate's step and the job still reports the same context, green. A required context is therefore necessary and not sufficient, and this file asserts the necessary half.
owner_ruling_2026_09_10: THE THREAT-MODEL QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and the answer removed two dimensions from this expectation rather than adding an exception for them. Owner ruling, 2026-09-10, quoted in substance and translated from German: 'I reset the settings deliberately. I am the only maintainer, or the main one. There are others, but they are rarely active. That is why this would be a blocker.' Measured: five accounts carry write access (four write/maintain, one admin), and the owner states the four are rarely available. So a mandatory approving review is not a control on this repository, it is a stop. WHAT THIS COST, stated because a green anchor must not be read as more than it is: `minimum_approving_reviews` and `require_last_push_approval` are gone from this file AND from `NON_NEGOTIABLE_FLOOR`, and they are NOT exemptions — a dimension outside the trust model is not a waived rule. The mechanism therefore proves nothing about independent human review, separation of duties, or protection against unilateral administrator action, and `docs/contracts/ratification-artifact.md` now says so in those words. WHO MAY DO THIS AGAIN: only the owner may AUTHORIZE a floor reduction; an agent may implement one. The distinguishable event is the owner's own review and merge of a conspicuously labelled trust-model change — not an agent's transcription of a chat message, and not a council record, which is evidence and never authorization. The verifier cannot authenticate that the owner meant it, and that limit is part of the record rather than hidden by it. THE BOUNDARY, which the mechanism cannot check: a floor reduction is legitimate only where the operating model CANNOT satisfy the floor — no second human exists — never where waiting is merely inconvenient. DECIDED BY: the owner on the policy; an AI council (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, 2 rounds each of two runs, blind peer review, 2/2 convergent on option (b)) on the implementation shape, which is council-decidable rather than owner-reserved. openai: 'Keeping those requirements hard-coded would make red mean the repository intentionally chose a different trust model, rather than the configured platform violated its policy. That is not a useful compliance signal.'
strict_status_checks_note: `strict_required_status_checks` STAYS in the enforced set and is currently NOT satisfied, which is deliberate. It read true before this work, true in the write of 2026-09-10, and false afterwards, and the owner's ruling covers reviewer availability rather than whether a branch may merge against a stale base — so it is collateral rather than part of the decision. Both council seats put it out of scope for the ruling and one added the constraint this file honours: approval of a trust-model change is NOT authorization to mutate the live ruleset, so nothing here was restored on the forge. The gate consequently reds on exactly this one dimension, which is a control pointing at a real gap nobody has argued for — the opposite of the noise a permanently unsatisfiable floor would have produced. Restoring it is one setting and needs no reviewer.
threat_model_note: SUPERSEDED IN PART by `owner_ruling_2026_09_10` above, and kept because a superseded record reads differently from a deleted one — this is what the question looked like while it was open. Its unconditional-bypass half still stands and is still enforced: `bypass_actors` was emptied on 2026-09-10 and that change held through the revert of the two approval dimensions. Original text follows. UNRESOLVED, and named rather than assumed. openai/codex-default made this an explicit condition: the contract must state whether repository administrators are inside the threat model. Measured 2026-09-10, `bypass_actors` carries `{actor_type: RepositoryRole, actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always}` and the acting account reports `current_user_can_bypass: always`, so every rule above is advisory for that actor. `allow_unconditional_bypass: false` records the council's answer for the mechanism's own surface — an unconditional bypass actor is a FAILURE — but whether the owner intends administrators as a deliberate root-of-trust escape hatch is an owner question this file cannot answer. Until it is answered the mechanism supplies process evidence, not a platform-enforced guarantee, which is what `docs/contracts/ratification-artifact.md` now says.
evaluation_note: The verifier evaluates the EFFECTIVE combination of every applicable ACTIVE branch ruleset, never a single ruleset by id or name. openai required this explicitly: ruleset 17749383 ('main protection') is what exists today, and assuming its id, its name, or that one monolithic ruleset carries every rule would make the check wrong the first time an administrator splits it.
revisit_if: The repository's governance model changes; or the default branch's protection moves back to classic branch protection (this file's evaluator reads rulesets, and `repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection` returned 404 on 2026-09-10); or the job that carries the ratification gate is renamed, in which case `required_status_check_contexts` names a context that no longer exists and the verifier reds until this file is corrected.
